parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.summary: Get Advanced Forecasting Rows of a Project
get.description: Get Advanced forecasting rows. Each page will have a maximum of 100 items.

parameters.name: budget_view_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the Budget View (also known as Budget Template). Required to return spread amount for other curves besides manual. Also required when column-based forecasting is enabled.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Array structure to filter the result of the advanced forecasting endpoint
Supported filter objects (with and without budget_view_id):
  - WBS segment item filter
    Structure:
      - id: <segment_id>
      - tier: <segment_tier>
      - type: 'segment'
      - values: <array of segment item ids>
  
    Example:
    `{"id": "23", tier: <segment_tier>, "type": "segment", "values": [2]}`

    URL example:
    https://app.procore.com/rest/v2.0/companies/<company_id>/projects/<project_id>/advanced_forecastings/rows?filters[][id]=23&filters[][tier]=1&filters[][type]=segment&filters[][values][]=2&page=1&per_page=100&budget_view_id=2

Supported filters only if budget_view_id is provided:
  - Actuals by date
    Structure:
      - id: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - code: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - type: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - values: [`<start_date>(YYYY-MM-DD)`, `<end_date>(YYYY-MM-DD)`, `<include_actuals_without_dates (boolean)>`].
    
    Example:
    `{"id": "date_range_for_actuals", "code": "date_range_for_actuals", "type": "date_range_for_actuals", "values": ["2021-01-01", "2021-01-31", false]}`

    URL Example:
    https://app.procore.com/rest/v2.0/companies/<company_id>/projects/<project_id>/advanced_forecastings/rows?filters[][code]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][id]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][type]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][values][]=2021-01-01&filters[][values][]=2021-01-31&filters[][values][]=false&page=1&per_page=100&budget_view_id=2

id.description: Identifier of the thing being filtered on. For a segment filter this is the WBS segment id; for a date-range-for-actuals filter it is the literal 'date_range_for_actuals'.

code.description: Filter code. Required for the date-range-for-actuals filter (set to 'date_range_for_actuals'); omit for segment filters.

tier.description: Tier of the Segment if applicable

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

data.description: Array of Advanced forecasting summarized rows

budget_line_item_id.description: Identifier of the budget line item this forecasting row belongs to. Null for rows that do not yet have a persisted budget line item.

wbs_code_id.description: Identifier of the WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code that scopes this forecasting row. Uniquely identifies the budget cost code combination being forecast.

start_date.description: First day the forecast applies to, in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Together with end_date it defines the span over which periods are distributed.

end_date.description: Last day the forecast applies to, in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Together with start_date it defines the span over which periods are distributed.

curve.description: The curve of the line item. For more information about the curve distribution visit https://support.procore.com/faq/how-do-procores-advanced-forecasting-curves-distribute-projected-cost-to-complete-amounts

forecast_to_complete.description: Total projected cost remaining (forecast to complete) for this line item, as a currency amount. This total is distributed across periods according to the curve.

periods.description: Per-period breakdown of the forecast-to-complete amount across the line item's date span.

period_date.description: Month this period applies to, in 'YYYY-MM' format.

amount.description: Currency amount of the forecast allocated to this period.

x-changelog.summary: Allow budget_view_id to enable support for all curves and the "Actuals by Date" filter in the GET Advanced Forecasting endpoint.
x-changelog.description:
Add support for all curves and the "Actuals by Date" filter in the GET Advanced Forecasting endpoint by allowing budget_view_id to be passed as a query parameter.
When budget_view_id is provided, the endpoint will:
1. Return spread amounts for all curves (including those beyond manual curves).
2. Apply the "Actuals by Date" filter if passed.

x-changelog.summary: budget_view_id may be required on GET Advanced Forecasting Rows.
x-changelog.description:
When column-based forecasting is enabled, GET Advanced Forecasting Rows now returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`
if `budget_view_id` is omitted. This parameter remains optional when column-based forecasting is disabled.

post.description:
Update Advanced Forecasting Rows.

When `async: true` and Budget Columns 2.0 is enabled, the response is `202 Accepted` with a single `receipt_id` that the client should use to poll `Check confirm budget version` API before re-fetching budget data. When `async: false` (default) or Budget Columns 2.0
is disabled, the response is `200 OK` with the updated rows.

async.description: Request asynchronous processing. When `true`, Budget Columns 2.0 must be enabled or the request will return `422`. On success returns `202 Accepted` with a single `receipt_id` that the client should use to poll `Check confirm budget version` API before re-fetching budget data.

budget_view_id.description: Unique identifier for the Budget View (also known as Budget Template). Required when column-based forecasting is enabled and the update changes forecasting data (period amounts/percentages, the curve, or the start/end dates that reshape periods); used to scope the update to the correct spreadable column. Not required otherwise.

x-changelog.summary: Added async support to Advanced Forecasting Bulk Update endpoint
x-changelog.description:
The POST Advanced Forecasting rows endpoint now accepts an optional `async` boolean parameter.
When `async: true` and Budget Columns 2.0 is enabled, the response is `202 Accepted` with a single `receipt_id`
representing the last processed event. When `async: false` (default) or Budget Columns 2.0 is
disabled, the standard synchronous response is returned.
